nameStory: Martha's Pennant honors Martha Wadsworth, an entomologist who contributed to our understanding of dragonflies. Like other pennants, this dragonfly gets its name from the way males perch conspicuously on vegetation tips, holding their wings like colorful flags fluttering in the breeze.
description: Martha's Pennant is a medium-sized dragonfly in the skimmer family, known for their habit of perching openly on prominent spots. These dragonflies have the typical sturdy build of skimmers, with broad-based wings and robust bodies. Males and females show different coloration patterns, with males typically developing more vibrant colors as they mature. Like other pennants, they're active fliers that dart out from perches to catch prey or chase rivals.

idTips.label: Wing Pattern
idTips.description: Look for distinctive dark markings or bands on the wings that help distinguish this species from other pennants in the area

idTips.label: Male Coloration
idTips.description: Mature males develop bright colors on their bodies, often with pruinescence (a waxy, powdery coating) that gives them a chalky or frosted appearance

idTips.label: Perching Behavior
idTips.description: Watch for their habit of perching prominently on tips of vegetation, returning repeatedly to the same favorite spots after brief flights

idTips.label: Body Size
idTips.description: Medium-sized among dragonflies, with a sturdy build typical of skimmers rather than the delicate frame of darners or clubtails

idTips.label: Flight Style
idTips.description: Strong, direct flight with frequent returns to perching spots, often hovering briefly before landing

habitat: Martha's Pennant frequents ponds, slow streams, and marshy areas with abundant emergent vegetation like cattails and sedges. They prefer sunny, open water areas where males can establish territories and find good perching spots on plant tips. Look for them around the edges of wetlands where there's a mix of open water and vegetated shoreline.

seasonality.spring: Adults begin emerging in late spring, with newly emerged individuals often appearing pale and less distinctly marked as they mature.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when mature adults are most visible, with males establishing territories and engaging in mating flights over suitable wetland habitats.
seasonality.fall: Activity continues into early fall, though numbers decline as the season progresses and temperatures drop.
seasonality.winter: No adult activity; the species overwinters as nymphs (immature forms) in pond and stream bottoms, hidden in mud and debris.

funFact: Dragonflies like Martha's Pennant are incredible aerial hunters with a 95% success rate when catching prey - making them more successful than sharks, lions, or any other predator on Earth!
confusionNotes: Martha's Pennant can be confused with other pennant species like the Calico Pennant or Halloween Pennant. Focus on the specific wing patterns and male coloration - each pennant species has distinctive markings that act like fingerprints once you learn to spot the differences.
contextualKnowledge: The 'pennant' name comes from their resemblance to small flags when perched, but don't confuse these dragonflies with the unrelated pennant butterflies. Pennant dragonflies are all in the genus Celithemis and share similar behaviors despite their different colorations.
compareHints: Among the pennant species, Martha's Pennant has its own unique wing pattern that separates it from the Calico Pennant's spotted wings, the Halloween Pennant's orange and brown bands, and the Banded Pennant's distinct banding. Pay close attention to wing markings and male body coloration - these are the most reliable ways to distinguish between the different pennant species in New England.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Among the pennant dragonflies, the calico has the most irregular, patchy wing pattern compared to its relatives.

Among its pennant relatives in New England, the Halloween Pennant is the only one with bright orange wings - the Calico Pennant has clear wings with dark markings, while the Banded Pennant has amber wings but lacks the extensive orange coloration.
Among the pennant dragonflies, the Banded Pennant stands out for having the most sharply contrasted black and clear wing pattern.
